## Design

### 2026-11-01: ![wiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5cf10048d64afed6d9dd95efd86010fd02f83254ee8029e6218935f891cbf1ac.png)

**3h**

![wiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5cf10048d64afed6d9dd95efd86010fd02f83254ee8029e6218935f891cbf1ac.png)
I started working on the schematic. I'm going to be using a Raspberry Pi Pico and a TFT display, which I just put into an 8-pin header. The wiring wasn't as bad as some of the other projects.

![betterwiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/e18d7acf28442f0f63e7e1b939ae139a9253907b248023ca2a71b37203852818.png)
I realized after wiring everything up that I could flip the orientation of the 8-pin header, so I flipped it, and now there are much fewer wires overlapping each other, and everything looks much cleaner.

![pcb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/0a55933976e56e796377d848f5da239010b7a328cf91dc6c5ac72128724224df.png)
I then chose the footprints for each component and put them into the PCB designer. This part was easier than the schematic, since all of the ratlines were already in place. I just connected all of them and made a back-layer copper fill to ground all of the necessary connections.
